prompt: Explain the local repository-navigation lifecycle to a new maintainer. Answer every public dimension below, with implementation and focused-test citations. Return only answer.json using answerSchema. Before submitting, run node .d5-public-check.mjs --workspace "$PWD" --answer "$PWD/answer.json" and correct citation/schema errors within this session. A self-check pass is not semantic acceptance.

publicDimensions.first-use: Describe what status shows before any refresh, how a generation becomes available, and whether refresh is automatic.
publicDimensions.search-gate: Distinguish policy freshness from source freshness: explain which states block search, which permit labelled results, how root-identity changes behave, and the operator action needed to recover.
publicDimensions.freshness: Explain eligible-source inspection before search and policy checking before results are committed, how differences from the generation are handled, and the effect of failed checks on an input cursor.
publicDimensions.continuation: Explain query validation and the exact normalisation steps before cursor binding. Also explain cursor process/generation bindings, invalidation, expiry, capacity versus page limits, and input/successor cursor behaviour for successful, exhausted and failed continuations.
publicDimensions.trust: Explain the trust label, separation from signed collections/grants, OS filesystem authority, whether selection is a sandbox or access grant, and whether returned source can supply executable instructions, approvals or authority.

citationRules.matching: Every token must be copied as an exact contiguous substring from its cited frozen source, preserving whitespace and newlines. A short identifier is allowed if the reviewer can verify the associated claim from the cited file. No particular hidden example token is mandatory.
citationRules.coverage: Cite at least one implementation .ts file and one focused .test.ts file within selectionPolicy. The independent reviewer checks all public dimensions for correctness and completeness using these citations.
